summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted one day after discharge due to fever, leukocytosis, and abdominal pain, concerning for a urinary tract infection. He has a chronic indwelling Foley catheter and a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs. Urine cultures grew pan-sensitive Proteus and multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, prompting a switch from ceftriaxone to ciprofloxacin. His mental status and symptoms improved with appropriate antibiotics. Constipation recurred, but resolved with continued aggressive bowel regimen after a bowel movement on hospital day 4. His blood cultures remained negative, and chest imaging showed atelectasis without pneumonia. Lisinopril was restarted for blood pressure control, and he was discharged to a rehab facility on a full course of ciprofloxacin and optimized home medications.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Delirium due to conditions classified elsewhere
Hyperplasia of prostate, unspecified, with urinary obstruction and other lower urinary symptoms (LUTS)
Infection with drug-resistant microorganisms, unspecified, with multiple drug resistance
